newsitem.title: USA: Zell's office REIT IPO well-received.
newsitem.headline: Zell's office REIT IPO well-received.

text.p: Shares in Equity Office Properties Trust, which is controlled by Chicago financier Samuel Zell, jumped more than 20 percent Tuesday when they began trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Stock in the company, which has the largest office property portfolio of any publicly traded company, added $4.625 to $25.625 in late morning on its first day of trading.

The offering of 25 million shares, which represents about 15.6 percent of the company, had been expected to attract investors because of the track record of Zell, its chairman, the size and quality of its portfolio of properties and the recent popularity of real estate investment trusts, or REITs.
"People say it's the star quality of Zell," Kenneth Campbell, chairman of CRA Real Estate Securities, a money management firm dealing in real estate securities, said before the company went public.
"I think it's really a vision of a company that is in scale and scope like nothing that's really come down the pike."
Equity Office's portfolio includes 90 office properties totalling about 32.2 million square feet. The portfolio also includes 14 stand-alone parking lots.
In 1996, the company's predecessors had $508 million in revenues, according to prospectus materials for the offering.
The company has the largest office portfolio, in terms of revenues and square feet, of any publicly traded U.S. company, its prospectus said.
It said proceeds from the offering are to be used to pay down debt, which totalled about $1.6 billion as of March 31.

In terms of scope, the properties are in 47 markets, giving it a national profile, unlike most of larger REITs, which are mostly regional in nature, said Robert Natale, analyst at Standard & Poors Equity Group.
Its properties were 92.5 percent occupied as of April 30.
REITs, which pay out most of their taxable income to shareholders to preserve their special tax status, are also an attractive place for investors who focus on total return, Natale said.

Analysts noted that Zell has a strong track record with two other real estate investment trusts -- Equity Residential Properties Trust, an apartment REIT, and Manufactured Home Communities Inc., an operator of mobile home communities. Zell is chairman of all three REITs.
"People think Zell is able to buy things at attractive prices," said David Linn, analyst at McDonald & Co. Securities.
